Key Research Thinking Patterns: Signal Processing: The researcher employs signal processing techniques, such as the Hirschman Transform, Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), and Hilbert Transform, to analyze and process signals in various domains, including medical imaging and video compression (e.g., the Hirschman Transform demonstrates superior quantization performance relative to the DCT and H.264 8×8 integer transform).

Image Processing: The researcher utilizes image processing techniques, such as Morphological Closing, Connected Components Labeling, and Bicubic Interpolation, to analyze and process images in various domains, including medical imaging and computer vision (e.g., the study demonstrates the effectiveness of MPM in reducing end effects and oscillations in the backbones of unforced harmonic oscillators).

Machine Learning: The researcher applies machine learning techniques, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and U-Net Architecture, to analyze and process data in various domains, including medical imaging and computer vision (e.g., the study uses YOLOv4 for object detection).

Analytical Signal Processing: The researcher employs analytical signal processing techniques, such as the Mirror Periodic Method (MPM) and Hilbert Vibration Decomposition (HVD), to analyze and process signals in various domains, including structural dynamics and biomedical engineering (e.g., the study demonstrates the effectiveness of MPM in approximating analytic-signal backbones of unforced harmonic oscillators)
Summary Description: Joseph Havlicek is a researcher with expertise in signal processing, image processing, and machine learning. His work focuses on developing novel techniques for analyzing and processing signals and images in various domains, including medical imaging, video compression, and computer vision. He has made significant contributions to the development of the Hirschman Transform, a new 2D separable 8×8 transform that demonstrates superior quantization performance. His research also explores the application of machine learning techniques, such as CNNs and U-Net Architecture, to analyze and process data in various domains. Additionally, he has worked on analytical signal processing techniques, such as MPM and HVD, to analyze and process signals in structural dynamics and biomedical engineering.
